messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95 latency breach for customer Nightingale Health (eu-west-1) — dedicated pool 'ng-eu-west-001'. Current p95 1.9s (SLO 1.2s). Spike started ~2024-11-13T21:07Z. PagerDuty: paging oncall.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: paged maria (oncall) — escalation level: page.

maria: I'm on it, joining warroom. pulling up dashboards and logs.

sam: quick snapshot: GPUs at 98% on ng-eu-west-001, queue depth climbing, qcache miss rate +600%.

nora: Customer impact: Nightingale ingestion jobs are timing out, several B2B customers reporting API 504s. CS alerted them and they're watching.

cheng: posting recent trace snippet: ```[2024-11-13 21:08:12] req_id=abcd1234 model=redwood-13b qcache_miss=1 elapsed=0.82s```. Also seeing KV cache eviction spikes coincident with tenant 'nightingale-analytics' batch window.

ops_bot: Autoscale check: pool ng-eu-west-001 at 80/80 GPUs (reserved capacity). Scaling blocked by reserved allocation limit. No spare nodes in eu-west-1.

maria: Immediate plan: 1) isolate noisy tenant with throttle route; 2) rollout trimmed model variant for that tenant; 3) warm failover to eu-central if needed; 4) evict tenant from shared pool as last resort. Starting step 1 now.

sam: Creating temporary route: `route add --tenant nightingale-analytics --policy throttle=0.25 --duration 30m` — applying.

ops_bot: route add applied for tenant nightingale-analytics. Throttle policy active. Expect effect in ~2-3 minutes.

nora: CS: told Nightingale support channel we're mitigating; they asked for ETA.

maria: ETA 10-15m to see p95 drop after throttle. I'll monitor p95/p99 and error rate.

sam: p95 down to 1.3s after throttle, qcache_miss reduced ~60%. Nice.

maria: Next step: model fallback for that tenant to `rw-small-quant` (lower-latency). @cheng can you run a 50% canary?

cheng: deploying canary: `service deploy --tenant nightingale-analytics --model rw-small-quant --canary 50%` — started.

ops_bot: Canary rollout applied: 50% traffic routed to rw-small-quant for nightingale-analytics. Monitoring metrics.

nora: Customer prefers config changes over failover; CS confirms they accept canary approach.

sam: After canary: canary p95 1.10s, overall p95 1.25s. Looks promising. Keep canary for 15m.

maria: If stable, promote to full fallback. Also file reserved capacity request — we hit hard cap.

support_lead: Created support ticket INC-2024-934 and looped infra. Collecting prompt/trace set for postmortem.

maria: Handoff: I'm staying on for next 30m to monitor. @cheng capture KV eviction patterns and add notes to postmortem. @nora keep CS updates flowing. If p95 > 1.4s re-escalate to SRE lead.

incident-bot: Status: oncall maria took ownership at 21:10Z. Warroom channel created #warroom-nightingale-1719204444.

sam: Observed a secondary tail spike at 21:22Z correlated with tenant's scheduled batch job — overlapped with canary rollout. Recommend asking Nightingale to pause heavy jobs for short window.

nora: CS confirms Nightingale paused heavy ingestion jobs on request. They expect to resume after 22:00Z.

maria: Closing plan: 1) full model fallback if stable after canary; 2) submit reserved capacity change; 3) postmortem with timeline and root-cause hypothesis (KV evictions triggered by tenant batch). Assigning follow-ups now.

ops_bot: Full fallback executed at 21:35Z — all Nightingale traffic on rw-small-quant. Observed p95 0.95s. INC-2024-934 updated with mitigation steps.

maria: Thanks. I'll draft the postmortem, ping infra for the reserved capacity adjustment, and schedule architecture review with the customer. Marking customer-impact mitigated.

sam: :thumbsup:

cheng: I'll pull and attach eviction traces and model cache metrics to the postmortem. Noted the eviction TTL pattern and batch windows.

nora: Customer satisfied with immediate mitigation and requested a follow-up architecture review next week.

incident-bot: Incident resolved for Nightingale Health at 21:36Z. Warroom remains open for postmortem notes.
